welcomePage.intro: Hi, I’m Ernesto Linares, a fullstack developer with a strong interest in backend development using .NET technologies. I’m nearing the completion of my studies and am currently seeking a role where I can continue to grow and contribute as a developer. Here you’ll find a selection of projects of varying sizes, my CV, as well as a section about who I am.

aboutPage.introductionText: Hi, my name is Ernesto Linares, a 33-year-old web development student from Borås. I am currently studying at EC Utbildning in Gothenburg — a .NET program focused on full-stack development. Programming is a completely new career path for me, and it has been a very rewarding change so far. I have always been drawn to problem-solving and creative work, and programming combines these in a great way. Recently, I have also discovered game development through Unity, where I see an opportunity to apply my C# skills in a more creative and playful way. It has quickly become a hobby that I am very enthusiastic about continuing to develop alongside my studies. I will graduate in June and have now started looking for a developer role, with a particular focus on backend.
aboutPage.traitsText:
I like to think strategically and come up with creative solutions — especially when things get complex. I get excited about new ideas and figuring out how things can work better.

Sometimes I rush to finish the big picture — but I've learned the value of slowing down, staying focused, and following through on the details. I’m confident, rarely shaken by setbacks, and enjoy taking initiative and moving things forward.

portfolioPage.ventixeDescription:
This project is a Minimal Viable Product (MVP) for an event booking system. The frontend was built using React, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript, while the backend is developed in C# using a microservices architecture.

Communication between services is handled via RESTful APIs. The entire project is under version control with Git, with microservices deployed on Azure Web App and the frontend hosted via Azure Static Web App.

The application uses SQL LocalDBs created through a code-first approach with Entity Framework, and includes user authentication and authorization handled by ASP.NET Identity. 

 Check out the code at Github https://github.com/MvpVentixe
portfolioPage.alphaDescription:
The goal of this project was to create a system inspired by an ERP platform, where users can manage projects, team members, and related tasks. The application is fully backend-rendered using ASP.NET MVC, with a structured layered architecture.

It includes a repository layer and a business logic layer, where interfaces and base classes are used to separate concerns and promote maintainability. This is an ongoing project that I plan to continue developing as I deepen my understanding of ASP.NET MVC and clean architecture principles.
portfolioPage.portfolioDescription:
This website is my personal portfolio, fully designed and built from scratch to showcase my projects and skills. It was developed using React, TypeScript, and Vite, styled with Bootstrap and custom CSS.

The design process started with wireframing in Figma, followed by responsive implementation and component structuring. This site also includes UI animations, routing via React Router, and accessibility considerations. It reflects my interest in frontend development and my evolving attention to design, usability, and performance.
portfolioPage.gymCoachDescription: Developed a mobile-first fitness tracking application using React and IndexedDB (Dexie.js), designed for a fully offline-first experience. Implemented structured data models for exercises, sessions, and workout history, with a focus on intuitive session tracking and history visualization. Integrated i18n (internationalization) to support multiple languages. Emphasized scalable client-side architecture, responsive UI, and efficient local data management without backend dependencies. The application has also been tested by users in my network and appreciated for its simplicity and ease of use.
portfolioPage.workerService: Developed a modular full-stack system simulating a real-world printer integration architecture. The ASP.NET MVC frontend is structured into three independent modules (partials), each representing a separate backend service. The cloud-hosted backend handles job creation and persistence in a SQL Server database, with capabilities to request printer status, job status, queue information, retries, and job cancellation. Communication with the frontend is performed via REST APIs using JavaScript, rather than traditional MVC controller binding. A long-running .NET Worker Service acts as the core processing engine. It continuously polls the database for new jobs, transforms them into printer-compatible JSON, and communicates with a local network printer over TCP. The frontend module connected to this service provides real-time, read-only insights using SignalR over an SSH tunnel. The system includes a simulated printer backend for testing, supporting state changes such as ink levels, maintenance cycles, and online/offline modes. The solution is containerized with Docker, includes logging, and is validated with xUnit testing. Currently under Development.
